## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

Four independent stores, none following from another — each is its own bearer:

- `SensorPermissionLaunchStoreImpl` — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/permission/SensorPermissionLaunchStoreImpl.kt (and its interface `SensorPermissionLaunchStore` in the same package)
- `ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStoreImpl` — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/connectivity/permission/ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStoreImpl.kt (implements `ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStore`, core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/connectivity/ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStore.kt)
- `ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStoreImpl` — app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/connectivity/permission/ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStoreImpl.kt (implements the same `ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStore` interface)
- `PhoneNavigationStateStore` — app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/ui/navigation/PhoneNavigationStateStore.kt (no interface; called directly)

## Trigger

`isFirstLaunch()`/`recordLaunch()` are called from `SensorPermissionManager.onLaunch` and
`SensorPermissionManager.isFirstLaunch` (app-wear), and from
`ConnectivityPermissionManager.onLaunch` (core-domain); `save()`/`restore()` are called from
`PhoneNavigator` (app-phone) — `restore()` from `PhoneNavigator`'s `backStack` property
initializer, `save()` from every one of its navigation methods (`toRaceDetail`, `toProfile`,
`toPasteResult`, `toImportPreview`, `toPasteError`, `backToPasteResult`,
`toRaceDetailAfterImport`, `back`) through `publishCurrent` — observed.

## Today

`SensorPermissionLaunchStoreImpl.isFirstLaunch/recordLaunch`, both
`ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStoreImpl.isFirstLaunch/recordLaunch`, and
`PhoneNavigationStateStore.save/restore` all call `SharedPreferences.getBoolean`,
`getString`, or `edit().apply()` directly in a plain (non-`suspend`) function, on
whatever thread the caller runs on — the caller's own coroutine or, for
`PhoneNavigator`'s `backStack` property, the constructor's thread. None of the four
declares `suspend`, and none moves the read or write onto `Dispatchers.IO`, unlike
`RaceRepositoryImpl`, `ProfileRepositoryImpl` and `WatchHistoryStoreImpl` in
`:core-data`, which each wrap their Room access in
`withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { … }`.

Two of the four already have a caller that cannot simply await a `suspend` version
as written:

- `SensorPermissionManager.isFirstLaunch()` is itself a plain (non-`suspend`) public
  function that returns `launchStore.isFirstLaunch()` directly; its own caller,
  `SensorPermissionViewModel`, does call it from inside `viewModelScope.launch { }`,
  but `SensorPermissionManager.isFirstLaunch()`'s own signature has no `suspend` to
  carry the awaited call.
- `PhoneNavigator` reads `stateStore.restore()` once, in the property initializer of
  its `backStack` field (`private val backStack: MutableList<PhoneDestination> =
  restoreBackStack()`), which runs during construction and cannot itself suspend;
  and every navigation method (`toRaceDetail`, `toProfile`, `back`, …) is itself a
  plain function that writes through `stateStore.save(...)` synchronously, with no
  coroutine scope of its own to launch onto.

## Expected

`isFirstLaunch`, `recordLaunch`, `save` and `restore` are `suspend` on all four
stores, and each moves its `SharedPreferences` access onto `Dispatchers.IO` inside
its own body (R24), the way the `:core-data` repositories already do.

Two second gaps follow from that change, on the two callers move 5 found unable to
accept it as written:

- `SensorPermissionManager.isFirstLaunch()` becomes `suspend` itself, so it can
  await the store's now-`suspend` `isFirstLaunch()`; its only caller already runs
  inside `viewModelScope.launch { }` and accepts the change without further work.
- `PhoneNavigator` needs a way to obtain the restored stack and to persist a new one
  without a `suspend` constructor and without a `suspend` navigation API: either it
  is handed its own `CoroutineScope` to launch `save` and `restore` on, with the
  `backStack` property built synchronously from a fallback and corrected once the
  restore completes, or its construction and every navigation method become
  `suspend` and every one of its callers (the phone `ViewModel`s and `MainActivity`)
  is adapted to call them from a coroutine. Which of the two is not this report's
  call — it is confirmed here so the split accounts for it.
